answers.answer: Shuffle all four III cards and place them face down at the bottom; shuffle all nine II cards and deal five face down above them; shuffle all three I cards and deal one face down on top. Return unused I and II cards to the box unseen.
answers.evidence: Setup: Conflict Deck construction; all used cards stay concealed.

answers.answer: Four-player: score starts at 1; two Agents start on the Leader and the third (Swordmaster) beside the board; three troops start in the garrison; take 1 water. Three-player: score starts at 0; the same Agent and troop setup; take 1 water.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 6: score is 1 in a 4-player game, otherwise 0; three Agents; three garrison troops; take 1 water.

answers.answer: Yes, you may Reveal while Agents remain, but after Revealing you take no further turns that phase. Reveal effects come from cards remaining in hand and revealed on the Reveal turn, not cards played on Agent turns. At Clean Up, all cards in front of you from Agent and Reveal turns go to your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Agent turns are optional; once Revealed, turns are skipped; Reveal Cards/Resolve Reveal Effects/Clean Up.

answers.answer: You must pay the destination cost before resolving the space or played card, so that card’s Agent-box effects and the destination’s effects cannot fund their own entry cost. A card sends only one Agent using one chosen icon. A card with no Agent icons cannot be used for an Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure, Agent Turn: pay costs before effects; choose only one Agent icon; no Agent icons means Reveal only.

answers.answer: At a Combat space, deploy the three troops recruited this turn plus at most two of the four already in the garrison, for up to five. At a non-Combat space, no units can be deployed. Recruited troops come from your supply and are placed in your garrison until deployed.
answers.evidence: Actions: Recruiting & Deploying Units; Combat spaces allow current-turn recruits plus up to two from garrison.

answers.answer: A Spy Agent icon lets you send an Agent to any space connected to a post where your Spy is; you do not recall that Spy. Infiltrate recalls a Spy at a connected post to bypass another player’s Agent, not your own. Gather Intelligence recalls a connected Spy to draw a card, chosen immediately after Agent placement and before space or card effects. One Spy cannot pay both; two different Spies may be recalled for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence respectively.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Spies & observation posts; Gather Intelligence timing and distinct Spy limits.

answers.answer: Strength is 11: two troops give 4, one sandworm gives 3, and four revealed swords give 4. If your last unit is removed, your strength becomes 0. With no unit in the Conflict you cannot play Combat Intrigue.
answers.evidence: Actions: Strength; Phase 3 Combat Intrigue requires a unit in the Conflict.

answers.answer: Yes. Passing does not stop you from playing later if an opponent acts; the window closes after all players involved in Combat pass consecutively. After rewards, troops return to their supply, sandworms to the bank, and Combat markers reset to 0.
answers.evidence: Phase 3: Combat Intrigue; Combat cleanup.

answers.answer: In either game, two tied for first each get the second reward; nobody wins or takes the Conflict card. In a four-player game, if exactly two tie for first, remaining players compete for the third reward; in a three-player game there are no other rewards. A player with 0 strength gets no reward.
answers.evidence: Phase 3: Resolve Combat; Combat ties; Strength.

answers.answer: One or more sandworms double rewards once; two worms do not quadruple them. Taking control of a location and battle icons on a Conflict card cannot be doubled. If a reward lets you pay 3 spice for 1 VP, doubling lets you pay a second time: pay 6 spice total to gain 2 VP, or pay only once for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Actions: Sandworm Reward Doubling: control and battle icons excluded; may pay cost again for doubled reward.

answers.answer: After winning, take the Conflict card face up into your supply, then check it against another face-up Conflict or Objective card there. A matching pair must be flipped face down for 1 VP. In Endgame, a wild icon may match any one of the three icons in your supply; flip the pair for 1 VP.
answers.evidence: Actions: Battle Icons; Phase 3 winner’s ordered card procedure.

answers.answer: At 2 Influence, gain 1 VP; lose it below 2 and regain it upon returning to 2. At 4, gain the printed track bonus, which is kept after dropping below 4 and earned again on returning to 4. The first to 4 also gets the Alliance and 1 VP, which is retained only while holding it. Tying the holder does not steal it; a challenger must rise above the holder.
answers.evidence: Scoring / Victory Conditions: Faction Influence; Alliance VP differs from retained track bonus.

answers.answer: Spend Persuasion before, between, or after Reveal effects. You may pool sources for one card or split a source among cards. The Imperium Row replenishes immediately to five, so you may buy the replacement if you can afford it. Acquired cards go face up into your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Actions: Acquiring Cards; Resolve Reveal Effects.

answers.answer: At each Maker space without an Agent, add one spice in Makers; when you visit, take all accumulated bonus spice, including when choosing worms. Deep Desert costs 3 water and offers 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, two worms; Hagga Basin costs 1 water and offers 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one worm. Hooks are retained, not spent, and are required only when the effect specifies them. While the Shield Wall remains, worms cannot be summoned to Arrakeen, Spice Refinery, or Imperial Basin; worms go to the Conflict, never a garrison.
answers.evidence: Actions: Sandworms; Makers; Maker Hooks are not spent; Shield Wall protects the three named Conflicts.

answers.answer: At Recall, at the end of a round, 10+ VP or an empty Conflict Deck triggers Endgame. Players first may play and resolve Endgame Intrigue, then compare VP. Rulebook resource tiebreakers are spice, then Solari, then water, then garrisoned troops.
answers.evidence: Phase 5: Recall; Scoring / Victory Conditions: Game end and tiebreakers.

answers.answer: Shuffle the 20 standard contracts face down, reveal two face up, and put the remaining 18 face down in the bank. Shuffle four additional Intrigue cards into that deck and four additional Imperium cards into that deck. Shaddam is optional. The 10 contrasting-back Rise of Ix contracts stay out of standard CHOAM.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module: Setup changes; 10 contrasting-back contracts are a separate Rise of Ix set.

answers.answer: Without CHOAM, or with CHOAM after all contracts are taken, the contract icon gives 2 Solari. With CHOAM contracts available, take one face-up offer and replace it from the bank face up. Complete Harvest by visiting a Maker space and gaining the shown spice amount that turn; Immediate as soon as taken; Acquire The Spice Must Flow when you next acquire that card.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module: Taking contracts; Completing contracts.

answers.answer: No. You must hold a board-space contract when sending the Agent there, so one acquired afterward waits for a future visit. When completed, announce it, gain its rewards, flip it face down, and leave it in your supply.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module: Completing contracts; FAQ & Rulings: Contract completion is mandatory and must be held at placement.

answers.answer: Use one shared scoring Rival. It gets the Ornithopter Objective; the humans randomly receive the other two eligible Objectives. First Player is the human whose card shows the marker; turn order is First Player, Rival, other human. The Rival never Reveals.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Setup; Agent turns.

answers.answer: Ignore the occupied destination and reveal another Hagal card. A Place Spy card places no Agent: try the specified empty post; if none exists, ignore the placement; then reveal another card and continue the same Agent turn. Ignore normal space costs and effects, applying only Hagal effects. If the deck empties or Reshuffle appears, reshuffle immediately and continue.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Agent turns; Place Spy cards; Hagal deck reshuffle.

answers.answer: Omit Objectives whose 1–3P/4/6P marking does not match, shuffle the eligible cards, and give one random card face up to each player. The First Player marker on an Objective determines the first player. Shaddam may be used only with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 3–5; Shaddam Corrino IV is not used without CHOAM.

answers.answer: The bank’s Solari, spice, water, and sandworms are not limited; make convenient substitutions if they run out. If your troop supply is empty, you cannot recruit until troops return there. Resource payments go back to the bank.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 6–7: troops cannot be recruited when supply is empty; bank resources are not limited and payments return.

answers.answer: The five phases are Round Start, Player Turns, Combat, Makers, Recall. At Round Start reveal a Conflict first, resolve any control defense, then each player draws five cards. If Endgame is not triggered at Recall, recall Agents to Leaders, pass First Player clockwise, and start the next round.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: five phases; Phase 1 Round Start; Phase 5 Recall.

answers.answer: Yes, after paying entry and meeting requirements before effects, board-space, Agent-box, and Faction Influence effects may be taken in any order. No, the Influence gained from that visit cannot satisfy its own entry requirement because requirements are checked before effects.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn: pay costs and meet requirements before resolving; effects may be carried out in any order.

answers.answer: No. An arrow cost/effect can be used once per turn, except sandworm doubling of a Conflict reward. Most effects are mandatory; “may,” optional arrow effects, and the black-X trash icon are optional, while direct self-trash instructions are mandatory. Intrigue conditions and costs must be met to play it.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Arrows / paying costs; FAQ & Rulings: Mandatory effects and costs.

answers.answer: Place a Spy from supply on an unoccupied observation post. If you have none in supply, you may first recall one of your Spies for no effect. If the placement specifies an Agent-icon type, only a post connected to that specified icon is legal.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Spies & observation posts.

answers.answer: No. Infiltrate bypasses only another player’s Agent, never your own. Recalling a Spy still requires playing a card for an Agent turn. You may use two different Spies for Infiltrate and Gather Intelligence, but cannot recall two to Gather Intelligence on one placement.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Spies; FAQ & Rulings: Spies.

answers.answer: The controller gets the location bonus whenever any player visits, including themself: 1 Solari at Arrakeen or Spice Refinery, 1 spice at Imperial Basin. Winning its Conflict places your Control marker there, replacing the opponent’s. At reveal of a Conflict for a location you control, you may deploy one troop from your supply without an Agent visit.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Critical Locations & Control.

answers.answer: For a tie at second, each tied player gets the third reward; the winner keeps first reward and the Conflict card, and no further rewards are given. Tied third-place players get nothing. Three tied for first each get second reward, and nobody takes the card or receives other rewards.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Combat ties; Three tied for first.

answers.answer: In a three-player Conflict with three different positive strengths, first and second place receive their rewards; third receives nothing. A two-player game includes the Rival as the third competitor, so the same 2–3-player reward rule applies.
answers.evidence: Phase 3: Resolve Combat: player count determines paid ranks, including two humans plus Rival.

answers.answer: Plot Intrigue is playable on your own Agent or Reveal turn; Combat Intrigue only during Combat and only with at least one unit in the Conflict; Endgame Intrigue at game end. Keep Intrigues face down, separate from your deck, until played; after resolving, put them face up in an Intrigue discard pile. If the deck runs out, shuffle its discard into a new deck.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Intrigue cards; FAQ & Rulings: Draw timing.

answers.answer: No. An ordinary discard is a card of your choice from your hand, and cannot be Intrigue unless specified. The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from hand. At Secrets, each opponent with four or more Intrigues gives one selected at random.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Discarding, Intrigue cards; Actions: Trashing.

answers.answer: Trash effects may remove cards from hand, discard pile, or in play. Return ordinary cards to the box; return Reserve cards to their Reserve stack. Trashing is optional unless paying a cost or directed to trash itself. Trashing The Spice Must Flow does not remove its acquired VP.
answers.evidence: Actions: Trashing; FAQ & Rulings: Victory.

answers.answer: An acquire-box effect resolves once when you acquire the card. If you need to draw while your deck is empty, shuffle your discard into a new deck. Unused Persuasion cannot be carried; it is lost at the end of Reveal.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Acquire box; Actions: Acquiring Cards.

answers.answer: Cards played on Agent turns and cards revealed on Reveal are in play until Clean Up at the end of Reveal, unless trashed first. Fremen Bond cards can activate one another regardless of play order, provided each has one or more other Fremen cards in play.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: In play / Fremen Bond.

answers.answer: Recall Agent returns one of your other Agents on the board, not the Agent sent this turn; you may use the recalled Agent on a later Agent turn in the same round. A retreated troop goes from Conflict to garrison. “Retreat any number” can mean zero.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Recall Agent icon; Retreat; FAQ & Rulings: Combat and troops.

answers.answer: No. A freely chosen effect that grants two Influence means both with one chosen Faction. An Alliance icon requires holding that Faction’s Alliance token; a minimum-Influence effect requires meeting its stated threshold.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Influence.

answers.answer: If the holder loses Influence after being tied by two opponents, the holder chooses which formerly tied opponent receives the Alliance. If the holder falls to 3 or lower and nobody has 4+, return the token to the board and the former holder loses its VP.
answers.evidence: Scoring: Alliance loss; FAQ & Rulings: Alliance loss.

answers.answer: A card drawn during Reveal is immediately revealed and used this turn. A card drawn after Reveal is kept for next round, in addition to the five cards drawn then. A Plot Intrigue with a later Reveal effect stays face up until that effect is used, then is discarded.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Draw timing.

answers.answer: No. A “when you win” Intrigue cannot be played after tying for first because nobody wins. If received as a reward for an outright win, it may be played immediately.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Combat and troops.

answers.answer: If all four resource tiebreakers also tie, the player who most recently took a Reveal turn wins. Scores may exceed 12.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Victory.

answers.answer: No. Complete all held contracts for the same space with one Agent placement; contract completion is mandatory. It resolves as another effect of that Agent turn and may be ordered with space and Agent-box effects, but you must hold it when sending the Agent.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Contract completion is mandatory.

answers.answer: No. Shaddam does not start with set-aside Sardaukar contracts; his Sardaukar Commander ability permits choosing a set-aside Sardaukar contract when acquiring one. His Emperor of the Known Universe restriction takes effect immediately when Signet Ring sends an Agent and lasts for that turn only, not the round.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module: Shaddam FAQ clarification.

answers.answer: Feyd’s token starts on the leftmost space of his Leader’s Training track and remains on the rightmost space once it reaches it. Lady Jessica begins face up, not Reverend Mother Jessica. Reverend Mother Jessica may use her ability on the turn she flips.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Leader clarifications; FAQ & Rulings.

answers.answer: Yes, moving from 1 to 3 reaches 2; reaching 2 again later while moving up can trigger again after losing Influence. Moving down through 2 does not count. Clean Up moving Spacing Guild’s Favor from in play to discard does not trigger its discard ability; only discarding it from hand does.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Leader clarifications; FAQ clarification for Spacing Guild’s Favor.

answers.answer: Accept Contract uses Spice Trade access and always draws one card; its contract icon gives 2 Solari without CHOAM, takes a contract when CHOAM has offers, and gives 2 Solari if they are exhausted. It is non-Faction and gives no automatic Influence. Dutiful Service uses Emperor access, gives 1 Emperor Influence (counted once), and resolves the same contract icon. Thus only Dutiful Service automatically advances a Faction.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide; Faction status and shared contract icon rule.

answers.answer: Arrakeen: City icon, no cost, Combat yes; visitor recruits one troop and draws one card, while controller gains 1 Solari. Fremkit: Fremen icon, no cost, Combat yes; gain 1 Fremen Influence and draw one card. Research Station: City icon, costs 2 water, Combat yes; recruit two troops and draw two cards.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table: Arrakeen, Fremkit, Research Station.

answers.answer: Deep Desert is Spice Trade, costs 3 water, and offers either 4 base spice or, with Maker Hooks, two worms. Hagga Basin is Spice Trade, costs 1 water, and offers either 2 base spice or, with Hooks, one worm. Both also give all accumulated bonus spice when visited, including on the worm choice; Hooks are retained, not spent.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide; Actions: Sandworms and Maker Hooks.

answers.answer: Both options require City access, 2+ Fremen Influence, and no resource cost. Option one: take Maker Hooks if lacking them, recruit one troop, and gain 1 water. Option two: gain 1 water and optionally remove the Shield Wall. The second option gives no troop.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Sietch Tabr.

answers.answer: High Council is Landsraad access and not a Combat space; each visit costs 5 Solari. First visit takes an unoccupied Councilor seat and gives 2 Persuasion on every Reveal turn for the rest of the game. Subsequent visits give 2 spice, draw an Intrigue, and recruit three troops.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: High Council.

answers.answer: Swordmaster is Landsraad access, not Combat, and can be taken once per player per game. It costs 8 Solari before anyone gains Swordmaster and 6 after anyone has one, including a Rival; the third Agent is available this round and for the rest of the game. A Rival gaining it reduces the human cost to 6.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Swordmaster.

answers.answer: Imperial Privilege is Landsraad access, non-Combat; it costs 3 Solari and requires 2+ Emperor Influence. Its effects: you may discard an Intrigue to draw an Intrigue; recall one of your other Agents and draw a card. It gives no automatic Emperor Influence.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Imperial Privilege; Faction status intro.

answers.answer: Shipping is Spice Trade access, non-Combat, costs 3 spice and requires 2+ Spacing Guild Influence. It gives 5 Solari and 1 Influence with any one Faction; the Influence need not be with the Guild.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Shipping.

answers.answer: Gather Support is Landsraad access, non-Combat: choose to pay 0 or 2 Solari; recruit two troops, and if you paid 2 also gain 1 water. Spice Refinery is City access and Combat: pay 0 or 1 spice to gain 2 or 4 Solari respectively; its controller separately gains 1 Solari.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Gather Support and Spice Refinery.

answers.answer: Heighliner: Spacing Guild, 5 spice, +1 Guild Influence, recruit five troops; Combat yes. Desert Tactics: Fremen, 1 water, +1 Fremen Influence, recruit one troop, optionally trash a card; Combat yes. Sardaukar: Emperor, 4 spice, +1 Emperor Influence, draw an Intrigue, recruit four troops; Combat no.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Heighliner, Desert Tactics, Sardaukar.

answers.answer: Assembly Hall is Landsraad, no cost, non-Combat: draw an Intrigue and gain 1 Persuasion during your Reveal if your Agent is there. Espionage is Bene Gesserit, costs 1 spice, non-Combat: +1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw a card, place a Spy. Deliver Supplies is Spacing Guild, no cost, non-Combat: +1 Guild Influence and 1 water.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Assembly Hall, Espionage, Deliver Supplies.

answers.answer: Affected opponents move their Spy to an empty post not connected to your Agent’s destination that turn. False Orders may be played even if no enemy Spy is connected there. Ignore Litany Against Fear’s red box during Reveal, or when it gains an Agent icon and is played as an Agent card.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: False Orders; Litany Against Fear.

answers.answer: Opponents cannot acquire the removed card. You may acquire it by other means, but without the 1-Persuasion discount. If unacquired by the end of your next Reveal, remove it from the game.
answers.evidence: FAQ & Rulings: Manipulate.

answers.answer: The Rival starts with four cubes at the bottoms of Influence tracks, three troops in its garrison and the rest in supply, two Agents and Swordmaster beside the board, three Spies, and 1 water; score and Combat start at 0. Shuffle House Hagal retaining the 2P Reshuffle card. The Rival can trigger Endgame at 10+ VP and can win.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Setup; Rival wins at 10+ VP.

answers.answer: As soon as its Solari, spice, Intrigue cards, and water total reaches its printed Swordmaster threshold, it spends that amount and gets its third Agent for the current round. Spend Solari first, then spice, Intrigue cards, water; keep leftovers. Its third Agent is immediately usable.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Resources and Swordmaster.

answers.answer: After Swordmaster, it spends 7 Solari for 1 VP, or separately 7 spice, 3 Intrigue cards, or 3 water for 1 VP each set. It cannot spend a mixed total of seven resources for a VP.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Resources and Swordmaster.

answers.answer: The Rival chooses the Faction with least Influence, ties broken by leftmost priority icon. It gains the normal 2-Influence VP and Alliance VP, but does not get the 4-Influence track resource bonus. A numbered Hagal Influence icon means that position in the Rival card’s Faction priority list.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Resources and Swordmaster; Influence selection.

answers.answer: No. It chooses only the destination matching current conditions; if that one is occupied, it reveals another Hagal card, without using the other destination. Accept Contract/Shipping is selected by Guild Influence; Deliver Supplies/Heighliner by Conflict tier.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Agent turns.

answers.answer: Yes. At every Combat space the Rival deploys up to two available garrison troops even if the card recruits none, plus all troops recruited that turn. At noncombat spaces recruits go to garrison. An unmet 2+ Influence bonus is ignored and never prevents Agent placement.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Agent turns.

answers.answer: Unless specified, it uses the first available Faction observation post in priority order; if all four are occupied it ignores placement. Placing its third and final supply Spy recalls its other two and triggers its Scheme. Rivals never recall Spies for Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Spies and Schemes.

answers.answer: If the Scheme recruits troops before the Agent placement, and the Rival then visits a Combat space that turn, those troops deploy too. A Place Spy card with no legal post ignores placement, then immediately reveals another Hagal card and continues the Agent turn.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Agent turns; Spies and Schemes.

answers.answer: The Rival always takes accumulated bonus spice at a visited Maker space. With Hooks and a Conflict that permits worms, it summons one at Hagga Basin or two at Deep Desert instead of base spice. If it summons none, it takes base spice (Hagga 2, Deep Desert 4); without Hooks or at a protected Conflict it therefore takes base spice. Hooks are not spent.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Maker spaces; Actions: Sandworms.

answers.answer: At Combat start, if it has at least one unit deployed, reveal a Hagal card and add its bottom swords to strength. If Reshuffle appears, reshuffle and reveal again. Then humans have their normal Combat Intrigue window. A Rival with no unit gets no bonus.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Combat.

answers.answer: Yes. It gets normal control bonuses, defensive troops, battle-icon VP, Conflict rewards, and doubles rewards with worms. It always takes optional Conflict VP if it can pay or recall required Spies. It never takes contracts; a contract reward gives it 2 Solari even with CHOAM.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Combat.

answers.answer: During Resolve Reveal Effects, total and announce strength and set the Combat marker at any point; update it as needed during that turn. Above 20, flip the marker to its +20 side and start again from the beginning of the track.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Resolve Reveal Effects; Actions: Strength.

answers.answer: A Leader’s Signet Ring ability activates when you play Signet Ring on an Agent turn, not merely when you reveal it. Card text can override normal game rules.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 3; Overview: Cards of any type can override usual rules.

answers.answer: A Recall Spy icon returns one of your Spies from an observation post to your supply, usually as a cost for a card effect. It does not automatically Infiltrate or Gather Intelligence; those are separate recalls without a card for their own effect.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Spies & observation posts.

answers.answer: The separate trash-an-Intrigue icon trashes one Intrigue of your choice from your hand. An ordinary discard instruction discards a card of your choice from your hand and does not allow an Intrigue unless specified.
answers.evidence: Actions: Trashing; Special Rules: Discarding.

answers.answer: Yes. When a sandworm doubles a Conflict reward that grants 1 freely chosen Influence, the doubled reward lets you gain 2 Influence with the same Faction or with two different Factions. By contrast, one effect granting two freely chosen Influence requires both with one Faction.
answers.evidence: Actions: Sandworm Reward Doubling; Special Rules: Influence.

answers.answer: The Hagal Signet Ring effect resolves the Rival’s printed Signet Ring ability. It does not need a human Signet Ring card or Reveal turn; the Hagal effect is the trigger for the Rival ability.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: follow the Rival card’s printed Signet Ring ability; Hagal Agent-turn effects include Signet Ring.

answers.answer: Maker Hooks icon: take a token from the bank only if it lacks one. Shield Wall removal works only if it has Hooks and the Wall remains; without Hooks ignore it, and if the Wall is already gone it has no further effect.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Rival Hooks and Wall icons.

answers.answer: Secrets is Bene Gesserit access, no cost, non-Combat. Gain 1 Bene Gesserit Influence, draw an Intrigue from the deck, and each opponent with 4+ Intrigues gives one chosen at random.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Secrets.

answers.answer: Imperial Basin is Spice Trade access, no cost, Combat yes. Visitor gains 1 base spice plus all accumulated bonus spice; its controller separately gains 1 spice. If visitor and controller are the same, that player gets both the visitor and controller gains.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide: Imperial Basin; controlled locations give visitor and controller effects separately.

answers.answer: Reveal the new Conflict face up next to the deck, on top of any Conflict cards remaining from previous rounds. Thus an unclaimed prior card remains beneath it. Reveal the Conflict first, then resolve defense, then each player draws five cards.
answers.evidence: Phase 1: Round Start.

answers.answer: Each human’s four Faction cubes start on the bottom spaces of their Influence tracks; Alliance tokens start on the marked areas of the four tracks, not with a player. Shield Wall token starts on the board below Spice Refinery.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 1 and 6; normal setup assigns no Maker Hooks token to a human.

answers.answer: First Player takes the first turn; play proceeds clockwise one turn at a time. A Reveal ends that player’s turns for the phase; in 3–4 players Player Turns ends when everyone has Revealed. Combat Intrigue starts with First Player and proceeds clockwise; each eligible player may play any number or pass. The window closes after all involved players pass consecutively.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Player Turns; Phase 3: Combat Intrigue.

answers.answer: The steps are Reveal Cards, Resolve Reveal Effects, Clean Up. Reveal effects may be resolved in any order, not card order.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Reveal Turn.

answers.answer: Shuffle each human’s 10-card starter and place face down in supply left of Leader. Without CHOAM, omit marked cards, shuffle Intrigue and Imperium decks separately face down, and deal five Imperium cards face up as Row. Put Prepare the Way and The Spice Must Flow in separate Reserve stacks. Combat marker starts at 0; three Spies, Councilor, and Control markers start in supply.
answers.evidence: Setup, steps 4 and 6; Initial card states.

answers.answer: Ordinarily acquire any of the five Imperium Row cards, Prepare the Way, or The Spice Must Flow. Costs are printed at each card’s upper right. Purchases using Persuasion happen during your Reveal turn.
answers.evidence: Actions: Acquiring Cards.

answers.answer: Yes. Ordinary Spy placement and Recall Spy icons are optional even if a legal move exists. Shield Wall removal is optional; once removed it returns to the box and cannot return later.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Spies & observation posts; Shield Wall.

answers.answer: The played card must have a matching normal Agent icon or its Spy Agent icon with your Spy at a connected post. A Spy connected to Shipping alone does not let a City-only card send an Agent there. If the card has the Spy Agent icon, the connected Spy permits that space without recalling it.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn; Special Rules: Spies & observation posts.

answers.answer: Yes. On your Agent turn you may first play a legal Plot Intrigue, and resources it grants before placement can pay the entry cost. Resources gained only after placement from the destination or played Agent card cannot pay that same cost.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: Plot Intrigue timing and entry costs.

answers.answer: No. In two-player play, once both humans have Revealed, skip them but continue the Rival’s Agent turns while it has Agents in supply. The Rival never takes a Reveal turn; Combat begins after both humans Revealed and Rival used all Agents.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure: two-player Player Turns.

answers.answer: The 22 spaces (icon; Combat?): Accept Contract—Spice Trade, No; Arrakeen—City, Yes; Assembly Hall—Landsraad, No; Deep Desert—Spice Trade, Yes; Deliver Supplies—Spacing Guild, No; Desert Tactics—Fremen, Yes; Dutiful Service—Emperor, No; Espionage—Bene Gesserit, No; Fremkit—Fremen, Yes; Gather Support—Landsraad, No; Hagga Basin—Spice Trade, Yes; Heighliner—Spacing Guild, Yes; High Council—Landsraad, No; Imperial Basin—Spice Trade, Yes; Imperial Privilege—Landsraad, No; Research Station—City, Yes; Sardaukar—Emperor, No; Secrets—Bene Gesserit, No; Shipping—Spice Trade, No; Sietch Tabr—City, Yes; Spice Refinery—City, Yes; Swordmaster—Landsraad, No.
answers.evidence: Board Space Guide table lists all standard 22 spaces with Agent access and Combat?.

answers.answer: At Round Start, when a Conflict is revealed for a location the human already controls, they may deploy one troop from supply directly to that Conflict; it is optional and needs no Agent visit. After rewards, all Combat markers reset to 0 before Makers.
answers.evidence: Phase 1: Round Start; Critical Locations & Control; Phase 3 cleanup.

answers.answer: Play one card from your hand face up in front of you and send one Agent from your Leader to a matching unoccupied board space. Resolve its Agent box, not Reveal box. You cannot reuse a card already in play or discard pile, or simply move an Agent already on the board; recall effects specifically return another Agent to the Leader.
answers.evidence: Agent Turn; cards and Agents must be played/sent as described.

answers.answer: The restriction applies immediately when he plays Signet Ring to send the Agent; he cannot postpone it by resolving board-space effects first.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Shaddam Corrino IV Leader clarification.

answers.answer: First gets first reward, second gets second, and third gets third; fourth gets none. The highest-strength player wins and takes the Conflict card, then checks battle icons.
answers.evidence: Phase 3: Resolve Combat; 4-player ranks; winner’s card procedure.

answers.answer: Players may choose a Leader or select one at random.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 3: choose, or select at random.

answers.answer: An ordinary draw comes from your own deck; if it is empty, shuffle your discard pile into a new deck and continue. You may not choose directly from your discard pile.
answers.evidence: Special Rules: Drawing cards.

answers.answer: Shuffle House Hagal and place the deck near the Rival, retaining the 2P Reshuffle card. Do not remove it.
answers.evidence: Required Rival Rules: Setup.

answers.answer: All four Maker Hooks tokens begin in the common bank; normal setup assigns none to a human. When acquired, a token moves from the bank to the player’s garrison.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 7.

answers.answer: Yes. If Combat Intrigue changes a participant’s deployed units or otherwise changes strength, adjust their Combat marker when that card resolves during the Combat Intrigue window. Use adjusted strength on the track for Combat rewards.
answers.evidence: Phase 3: Combat Intrigue: strength adjustment and resolve using adjusted strength.

answers.answer: Gain Solari, spice, or water from the bank. You do not take resources from another player’s supply.
answers.evidence: Setup, step 7: bank receives gains and paid resources return there.

answers.answer: Shuffle all 20 standard contract tokens face down, then flip two face up as offers on the board; place the remaining 18 face down in the bank. Players do not choose the offers or set a preset order; the shuffle determines the offers.
answers.evidence: CHOAM Module: Setup changes: shuffle face down, flip two face up, remaining in bank.
